messages.author: 6e0bce06355e4e6c
messages.subject: Wishart-alternative?
parts:
I read the following comment in one of Andrew's blog-posts:
Bob Carpenter says: (August 29, 2012 at 1:43 pm)
Our basic constraint strategy for Stan lets us put a uniform prior on the correlation matrix and whatever prior you want on the vector of scales.

This is exactly what I was looking for! I would like to specify uniform priors on the correlation matrix, yet without being very restrictive on the scales (as would happen with a Wishart); perhaps someone has a coded example or a better alternative? The model is intended for a large dataset, so something that samples relatively fast would be valuable too.

Marcel


parameters {
  vector[V] beta[N];
}

model {
  # prior on mu_beta -> reparametrized cf. pp. 104 in STAN 1.1.1 ref manual
  # prior on sigma -> Wishart alternative?
  for (n in 1:N){
    beta[n] ~ multi_normal(mu_beta, sigma) ;
  }
}

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Wishart-alternative?
parts:
On Monday, February 18, 2013 6:42:23 AM UTC-5, Marcel Jonker wrote:
I read the following comment in one of Andrew's blog-posts:
Bob Carpenter says: (August 29, 2012 at 1:43 pm)
Our basic constraint strategy for Stan lets us put a uniform prior on the correlation matrix and whatever prior you want on the vector of scales.

This is exactly what I was looking for! I would like to specify uniform priors on the correlation matrix, yet without being very restrictive on the scales (as would happen with a Wishart); perhaps someone has a coded example or a better alternative? The model is intended for a large dataset, so something that samples relatively fast would be valuable too.

You would need something like this:

parameters{
  corr_matrix[K] Sigma_corr;
  vector[K] Sigma_sd;
  ...
}
model {
  matrix[K,K] Sigma;
  Sigma <- diag_matrix(Sigma_sd) * Sigma_corr * diag_matrix(Sigma_sd);

  // prior on Sigma_sd
  // implicit: Sigma_corr ~ lkj_corr(1.0)
  beta ~ multi_normal(mu_beta, Sigma);
}

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Wishart-alternative?
parts:
Sigma_sd needs to be constrained to be positive,
as follows:

parameters{
corr_matrix[K] Sigma_corr;
vector<lower=0>[K] Sigma_sd;

...
}
model {
matrix[K,K] Sigma;
Sigma <- diag_matrix(Sigma_sd) * Sigma_corr * diag_matrix(Sigma_sd);

beta ~ multi_normal(mu_beta, Sigma);
}

This implicitly puts a uniform prior on the correlation matrix.
You can also shrink it toward the unit matrix by using lkj_corr().

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Wishart-alternative?

On Monday, February 18, 2013 7:11:25 PM UTC-5, Marcel Jonker wrote:
When I use the print() command, I see that sigma_sd is positive but this doesn't solve the problem. The error message is:
Exception: Error in function stan::prob::multi_normal_log(d): Covariance matrix is not positive definite. Covariance matrix(0,0) is 22.6177 (etc.)

I think someone else mentioned a problem like this. The correlation matrix is positive definite with probability one by construction, but it is possible that it is numerically singular. But Stan should just reject that proposal and continue. Are you saying the sampling stops?

Ben
